title: Immersed in microclimatic space: Microclimate experience and perception of spatial configurations in Dutch squares

findings.antecedent: spatial configurations (general)
findings.mechanism: People develop 'schemata' or 'cognitive maps' about urban places based on spatial layout and environmental cues.
findings.quote: people have microclimate "images" or "schemata" about urban places that relate to the spatial layout of place.

findings.antecedent: salient microclimate situations (especially windy ones)
findings.mechanism: Salient experiences get engrained in a person's memory, influencing long-term schemata.
findings.quote: long-term microclimate schemata are influenced by rather salient microclimate situations (especially windy ones in the Dutch situation) that get engrained in a person's memory

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'central open square area'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "too windy" (a) Central open square area

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of a tall building'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "too windy" (b) foot of a tall building

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'entrance of street canyon'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "too windy" (c) entrance of street canyon

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'passage'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "too windy" (d) passage.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'semi-enclosed area'
findings.consequent: perception of being 'comfortable in terms of wind'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations, preferring enclosed spaces.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "comfortable in terms of wind" (a) Semi-enclosed area

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of a low building'
findings.consequent: perception of being 'comfortable in terms of wind'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "comfortable in terms of wind" (b) foot of a low building.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'semi-enclosed area'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations, preferring enclosed spaces.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "comfortably sunny" (a) Semi-enclosed areas

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of a low building'
findings.mechanism: People assign certain microclimate characteristics to specific spatial configurations.
findings.quote: Places perceived to be "comfortably sunny" (b) foot of a low building.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration types with 'some sense of enclosure'
findings.mechanism: Preference for spatial enclosure and smaller scale places, consistent with proxemics research.
findings.quote: spatial types with some sense of enclosure were rated more positive than the spatial types like large open squares.

findings.antecedent: wind speed (measured)
findings.mechanism: Wind speed is a primary physical parameter influencing thermal comfort perception.
findings.quote: Wind speed was clearly the most important parameter in terms of people's experiences.

findings.antecedent: sun (shadow simulations)
findings.mechanism: Sun exposure is a primary physical parameter influencing thermal comfort perception.
findings.quote: Also the parameter "sun" was important.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'central open square surface'
findings.mechanism: Squares with H/W ratio < 0.25 exhibit 'isolated roughness flows' leading to higher wind speeds.
findings.quote: these areas indeed show higher wind speeds than the areas considered comfortable in terms of wind

findings.antecedent: H/W ratio of square < 0.25
findings.mechanism: Squares with H/W ratio lower than 0.25 show typical wind flow patterns that bring flows of wind higher speeds ('isolated roughness flows') to the central areas.
findings.quote: Squares that have a H/W ratio lower than 0.25 show typical wind flow patterns that bring flows of wind higher speeds

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'central open square surface'
findings.mechanism: People's perceptions align with actual wind conditions due to developed comprehension of wind climate.
findings.quote: user's assessments of the open square areas to be 'windy' matched well and that people have developed a good comprehension of the wind climate

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of a tall building'
findings.mechanism: Downwash effects around tall buildings cause higher wind speeds.
findings.quote: these areas indeed had higher wind speeds than the areas considered comfortable in terms of wind

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of a tall building' (Eindhoven point 4)
findings.mechanism: Wake of trees might suppress winds in that specific spot.
findings.quote: The measurements in place no. 4 in Eindhoven, however, showed only marginally higher wind speeds than places that were considered comfortable in terms of wind.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of a tall building'
findings.mechanism: People's perceptions align with actual wind conditions due to downwash effects.
findings.quote: the perception of people about these places being 'windy' is justified, both by the measurement results and other research.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'entrance of street canyon'
findings.mechanism: Street canyons act as wind funnels (venturi effects) and angular corners cause gusty winds.
findings.quote: clearly show higher wind speeds in our measurements than areas that are perceived comfortable in terms of wind.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'entrance of street canyon'
findings.mechanism: People correctly interpret spatial cues for wind climate in these types of spaces.
findings.quote: people often correctly read the cues for wind climate in these types of spaces.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'passage'
findings.mechanism: Passages act as strong wind funnels.
findings.quote: measurement results here were once more higher than the ones in the places considered comfortable in terms of wind.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'passage'
findings.mechanism: People's interpretations of passages as 'draftholes' are appropriate.
findings.quote: people's interpretations are quite appropriate.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'semi-enclosed area'
findings.mechanism: Semi-enclosed areas offer wind protection from three sides.
findings.quote: All the measurements taken in these areas showed indeed lower wind speeds than the ones taken in places considered to be 'windy'.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'semi-enclosed area'
findings.consequent: perception of being 'comfortable in terms of wind'
findings.mechanism: People's interpretation of this spatial cue has a high probability of being suitable.
findings.quote: people's interpretation of this spatial cue "semi-enclosed area" has a high probability to be suitable.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of lower buildings'
findings.mechanism: Lower buildings provide wind protection as part of cavity or wake areas.
findings.quote: The averaged measurements taken in two typical spots also show lower wind speeds than the places perceived 'windy'.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of lower buildings'
findings.consequent: perception of being 'comfortable in terms of wind'
findings.mechanism: People's assessment might be based more on reading spatial cues than the actual wind microclimate.
findings.quote: people's assessment might be based more on the reading of the spatial cues than the wind microclimate.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'semi-enclosed areas'
findings.consequent: match between perceived 'sunny' and actual sun exposure
findings.mechanism: People's perceptions do not sufficiently account for actual sun/shadow climate, relying more on the spatial setting.
findings.quote: total match of 62% indicated that people's perceptions of sun tend to be only partly appropriate, with still a large percentage unexplained.

findings.antecedent: spatial configuration type 'foot of lower buildings'
findings.consequent: match between perceived 'sunny' and actual sun exposure
findings.mechanism: Perception might be influenced by a friendly atmosphere or unconscious choice to stay in sunny spots, rather than objective sun exposure.
findings.quote: total match of 66% shows that people's perceptions of sun tend to be rather appropriate, with still quite a large percentage unexplained.

stimuli.description: Three Dutch urban squares (Spuiplein in Den Haag, Neckerspoel in Eindhoven, Grote Markt in Groningen) with varying spatial configurations and microclimates.

limitations: The findings represent only a small fraction of the relations between spatial and microclimate perceptions.
The research was conducted in a specific climate zone (temperate maritime North Western Europe), and results might differ in other climate zones.
The study did not investigate other places with very different sizes or spatial setups, which might yield different results or more spatial configuration types.
The cognitive map generated from one interview was normally not covering all parts of the square.
